svg.title: FROST Tomasulo back-end: allocation, execution, completion and commit
svg.desc: RV64GCBV Tomasulo out-of-order back-end. IF, PD and ID feed a four-bundle decoded queue into two-wide dispatch and INT/FP register renaming with twelve branch checkpoints and a speculative vtype tracker. Dispatch allocates entries in the 32-entry reorder buffer, four reservation stations (INT 16, MUL 4, FP 6, MEM 8), the eight-entry load and store queues and the four-entry vector memory table (VMT) in parallel. The four stations issue independently: INT issues up to two operations per cycle to two ALUs (with branches and JALR on pipe 0 and pipe 1 scanning the low eight entries); MUL feeds integer and carry-less multiply, a radix-4 divider and vector configuration (vset* on CDB slot 5); FP feeds a seven-stage FMA pipeline (add, subtract, multiply and FMA with a 16-entry result FIFO and one-cycle early forward wakeup to FP RS), a radix-16 divider and an FP engine for square root, conversions and misc operations; MEM feeds address generation and the Sv39 DMMU (16-entry DTLB, resident-hit and Bare bypass, backed by the shared 2,048-entry four-way L2 TLB with a 32-entry superpage side array and pointer-walk-cache PTW). The load queue holds a 512-entry, eight-byte L0 cache, checks store-queue forwarding and VMT range holds, and issues early load wakeups to INT and MEM stations before CDB broadcast. The store queue handles buffered cached and Normal stores, cbo.zero, Zicbom CMOs and head-ordered precise uncached stores. Ordinary buffered stores complete the ROB directly; store faults, SC results and LQ completions share the MEM CDB slot (slot 3). Seven arithmetic/config slots and MEM form eight fixed-priority CDB slots (MUL, MEM, ALU, ALU2, DIV, FP_DIV, FP_MUL, FP_ADD) broadcasting on two lanes; slot 6 carries the FP pipeline FIFO and yields to vector ROB-head VTOX, VTOF and VMEM completions. Up to two instructions retire in order, updating INT/FP register files, releasing committed stores and enqueuing committed vector arithmetic into the eight-entry post-commit VIQ. Serializing instructions and precise uncached stores hold the ROB head; a hardware misaligned-access engine assists misaligned cached DDR ops at commit; conditional branch, JAL and JALR mispredictions recover early. Matching A and S badges mark allocation and store-release paths. Arrows do not imply pipeline latency.

Selected logical paths; arrows do not imply pipeline latency. Decoded queue, L2 TLB, PTW, vector unit, MA engine and data router live in cpu_ooo.
